title: Stock Market Highlights, Oct 5: Sensex rises 472 pts to end at 72,382, Nifty settles at 22,555; ITC, Eternal lead gainers - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Sensex Today, Nifty 50 | Stock Market Highlights - Find here all the highlights related to Sensex, Nifty, BSE, NSE, share prices and Indian stock markets for 5 October 2026.

Benchmark equity indices Sensex and Nifty ended higher on Monday, as softer-than-expected US jobs data reduced expectations of aggressive monetary tightening by the US Federal Reserve, supporting risk appetite across emerging markets.

The 30-share BSE Sensex jumped 472.77 points, or 0.66 per cent, to settle at 72,382.47. During the day, it surged 722.23 points, or 1 per cent, to 72,631.93.

The 50-share NSE Nifty climbed 133.80 points, or 0.60 per cent, to end at 22,555.75.

From the 30 Sensex firms, ITC, Eternal, Bharti Airtel, Bajaj Finance, Adani Ports, ICICI Bank, Reliance Industries and Larsen & Toubro were among the major winners.

HCL Tech, HDFC Bank, Sun Pharma, Infosys and Asian Paints were among the laggards.

Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, was up 0.19 per cent to $102.4 per barrel.

Top gainers of Nifty 50: ITC (+4.81%), BSE (+4.28%), TMP (+2.90%), Bajaj Finance (+2.38%), Shriram Finance (+2.29%)

Top losers: HCL Tech (-3.52%), Max Health (-2.86%), HDFC Bank (-2.20%), Asian Paints (-2.16%)

NOICE, Instamart’s clean-food private brand, has announced an ambitious new phase of growth, with plans to double its base of food entrepreneur partners and expand its product assortment to over 500 products. The brand has also introduced a financing programme offering eligible entrepreneurs access to formal credit of up to ₹5 crore through partnerships with SIDBI, Axis Bank and InCred Finance.

India-EU trade agreement could generate more exports and jobs in labour-intensive sectors such as footwear, textiles, toys and processed products.

BPCL plans to raise up to $3 billion through an international bond sale, largely to fund its $2.8 billion Brazil offshore development.

Bharat Forge secures a long-term Pratt & Whitney Canada contract to manufacture aerospace engine components at its India facility.

Sumitomo buys 49% of HFE's Bidar SPV to develop a ~500 MWp wind-solar project with battery storage in India.

Crude oil futures slide on weak global cues, dropping ₹256 to ₹8,660/bbl as analysts cite weak demand and global trends.

Jupiter Wagons wins 41 MW/102.5 MWh BESS project in Uttarakhand; receives Letter of Award for 50 MW/200 MWh Jeerat project in West Bengal

Perspective on gold by Ashish Rajodiya, Head – Commodities, PL Capital.

“Gold slipped on Monday, with MCX gold at ₹1,49,150 per 10 grams, down ₹1,245, while silver held firmer at ₹2,26,050 per kg, up ₹173. Spot gold is hovering around $4,135 an ounce after losing more than 3% last week and about 6% over the past month. The metal is caught between two opposing forces. Friday’s weak US jobs report, with payrolls up just 29,000 against expectations of 90,000 and unemployment edging up to 4.2%, has pushed the odds of an October Fed rate hike down to about 18%, from near 70% earlier in the week. Yet that relief has done little for bullion, because Treasury yields are still sitting at multi-decade highs and a firm dollar keeps raising the cost of holding a non-yielding asset. The broader view is sideways, with the metal likely to stay range-bound between support at ₹1,45,900 and resistance at ₹1,51,500. The Fed’s October policy decision is the next trigger. A clear signal that the hiking cycle is over, along with easing yields, could lift gold toward the top of that range, while a hawkish tone or a fresh surge in yields would put the ₹1,45,900 floor to the test.”

Gold dips nearly 1% to ₹1.49 lakh/10g as strong dollar and yields cap bullion recovery, with global cues and US data in focus.

Mukesh Ambani’s Jio Platforms plans a $3.8 billion IPO on October 21, which would be India’s biggest listing, with shares expected to list October 28.

Sabari Constructions Technologies files IPO papers on NSE Emerge for a fresh 63 lakh shares, aimed at ₹160 crore for working capital and growth.

India’s steel consumption is expected to grow 7-8% or more in coming years, while global tariffs drive greater supply chain localisation and domestic investment.

MathWorks, the leading developer of mathematical computing software for designing engineered systems, today announced a collaboration with MapmyIndia Mappls, India’s leading advanced digital maps and deep-tech products and platforms company, to support automotive engineers developing and validating Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) for Indian road environments.

By integrating MapmyIndia’s high-definition (HD) maps with MATLAB, Simulink, and RoadRunner, engineering teams can simulate realistic road and traffic scenarios and begin system validation earlier in the development cycle. The integration enables engineers to create digital twins of Indian road environments, simulate complex traffic scenarios, and test ADAS controllers within a Model-Based Design environment.

GST Council may protect genuine buyers from losing input tax credit due to supplier defaults and widen credit eligibility for several business expenses.

Schneider Electric to acquire PTC for $22.6 billion, expanding AI-driven industrial software amid a race in factory automation.

AceVector Ltd stocks debut 11.5% lower after a ₹420 crore IPO, valuing the firm around ₹1,395 crore and bidding 4.93x.

Pharmaceuticals accounted for 88.8 per cent of healthcare M&A activity by value in September 2026, while investment activity in the private equity space was led by hospitals and healthcare technology, according to an Equirus analysis of the healthcare sector.

The healthcare sector saw three major M&A deals in September, with the pharmaceutical sector continuing to account for the bulk of transaction value during the month.
